request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now has a "Watched due" figure (`watched-due-total`). It adds up the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, and shows `0.00` when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This was a front-end-only change. The app already stored watches per user and loaded them with the sheet, so I didn't need to change the stored data, the server or the audit records.

- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` value adds up the due-totals of the watched people, using the same per-person due figures the other header totals use. Anyone whose due-total is n/a counts as zero, the same way the crew total treats them.
- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/header.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` input, shown next to "My reviews".

The total updates straight away when the user watches or unwatches someone, as well as when the sheet is reloaded.
